about: The explainer video's script: one line per scene, in order. `text` is what the captions show; `say`, where given, is what the voice says instead (numbers and names written for speaking). `visual` is the storyboard for the scene, for whoever builds or changes timeline.js. The voice is generated by narrate.py; each scene holds until its line has finished.

lines.text: This is stretto. It reads ahead of your agent.
lines.visual: Black. The three bars of the mark enter one after another, each starting before the last has finished (a stretto), and settle into the mark; the wordmark writes on; the tagline fades up. A slow push-in. Sound: the motif enters in three overlapping voices, in time with the bars.

lines.text: An AI agent works in turns. On every turn, a large model reads the whole conversation, then picks one next step: answer the user, or call a tool. Each turn costs seconds and thousands of tokens, and one task can take dozens of them.
lines.visual: Fly from the mark into a wide world: the customer (a chat avatar) on the left, the agent in the middle (an illustrated model: a glowing core that visibly 'thinks' each turn, reading a scroll of conversation that grows), the MCP server on the right (a cabinet of drawers: users, orders, products). Each turn: the agent thinks, a call card flies to the server along a path, a result card flies back. The camera pans along with the first call, then pulls back as turns repeat faster. A turn counter, a clock and a token meter climb in a corner HUD.

lines.text: But watch the turns closely, and many are decided before they begin. Here, the customer's record lists two orders, so the agent's next two turns will read those two orders. The tools made that choice, not the customer. The model just spends a turn typing it out.
lines.visual: Freeze; zoom through into the first result card (get_user_details) until it fills the frame: a user record with two order ids highlighted. Lines draw from each id to the next two calls, get_order_details(#W7a) and get_order_details(#W7b), shown as ghosted future turns on a turn timeline. A label: 'decided by the tools'. The customer's speech bubble dims.

lines.text: stretto sits between the agent and its tools, as an MCP proxy. When a result names what the agent will read next, stretto makes those reads at once, and they arrive inside the result the agent already asked for. The agent has them before it asks, so it skips those turns. There are no new tools, and the prompt doesn't change.
lines.visual: Pull back out. The stretto proxy (the mark as a lens or prism) slides in on the path between agent and server. The agent's call passes through it; stretto sends two lookups of its own to the server; their results clip onto the returning result card, which arrives as one bundle. Below, the turn timeline: turns 2 and 3 fade out and the later turns slide left to close the gap: 5 turns become 3. A tag: 'no new tools, same prompt'.

lines.text: It only ever reads. It never writes, so it can't change anything. When it guesses wrong, the agent gets a lookup it didn't need: a few extra tokens, and nothing else.
lines.visual: Close on the server: read drawers glow petrol; the write controls (cancel, exchange, refund) sit behind a lock that stretto's reach passes by. Then a wrong guess: a lookup the agent never uses drops into the agent's context as a few small tokens, and the world around it does not change.

lines.text: Where do the guesses come from? stretto records the agent's sessions, and counts what it read after each call, and where each argument came from. That becomes a flow: a small file of counts you can read, review and diff, like code. About ten sessions teach it most of what there is to learn.
lines.visual: A tilted flyover across a stream of recorded sessions: rows of calls scrolling past below the camera. Counts tick up on the transitions between calls; the stream condenses into a flow graph (get_user_details to get_order_details, with its probability, to get_product_details) whose edges thicken as counts arrive, and argument sources draw as dotted lines from result fields to the next call. The graph folds into a file icon, which opens as a code-review diff with a check mark.

lines.text: A lookup is made when the chance that the agent uses it, before its next write, clears a threshold set by two costs: a turn saved, and a lookup wasted. That comes to about thirty percent. No extra model is asked. stretto just counts.
lines.say: A lookup is made when the chance that the agent uses it, before its next write, clears a threshold set by two costs: a turn saved, and a lookup wasted. That comes to about thirty percent. No extra model is asked. stretto just counts.
lines.visual: A balance: on one pan, a saved turn (about 6,000 tokens); on the other, a wasted lookup (about 2,500). It settles, and a threshold line drops out of it at 0.3 across a vertical probability gauge. Candidate lookups slide in as chips with their chances (0.94, 0.61, 0.33, 0.12); those above the line light up petrol and fire, those below grey out.

lines.text: Live, on τ²-bench's retail and airline tasks, stretto cut Claude Sonnet 5's LLM turns by twenty percent, Claude Haiku 4.5's by twenty-two, and GLM-5.3's by twenty-eight.
lines.say: Live, on tau two bench's retail and airline tasks, stretto cut Claude Sonnet 5's L L M turns by twenty percent, Claude Haiku four point five's by twenty-two, and G L M five point three's by twenty-eight.
lines.visual: A clean chart stage: for each model, a bar of LLM turns without stretto, then the bar with it shrinks in, with its number counting: Claude Sonnet 5 −20.5%, Claude Haiku 4.5 −22.4%, GLM-5.3 −27.9%. Small print: τ²-bench retail and airline, 28 tasks; three trials for the Claude models. The camera drifts slowly.

lines.text: Telling the agent to batch its calls saved only three to eight percent. Even with that prompt in place, stretto cut about twenty percent more.
lines.visual: Split screen: left, 'a prompt: make independent calls at once', a small bar (−3.4% to −7.6%); right, 'the prompt, plus stretto', the bar drops much further (−17% to −23%). A reads-that-depend-on-results diagram flashes: the prompt can batch what the agent already knows; stretto reads what the results reveal.

lines.text: stretto is open source. Install it, run stretto init to put it in front of an MCP server, and it learns from your agent's own sessions.
lines.say: stretto is open source. Install it, run stretto init to put it in front of an M C P server, and it learns from your agent's own sessions.
lines.visual: A terminal slides up and types: stretto init --host claude-code -- npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem ./notes. Its printed next steps scroll. Around it, the earlier world reassembles in miniature: agent, stretto, server.

lines.text: stretto. Read ahead of your agent.
lines.visual: The world pulls back into the mark (the three bars), the wordmark and tagline; below: alexnodeland.github.io/stretto · open source, MIT. Sound: the motif, once, resolving.
